subject: Copywriting
subcategory: The Science of Storytelling in Ads
title: The Problem-Agitate-Solve Formula
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Problem-Agitate-Solve Formula.

hook.text: Got back pain? Imagine another year of it. Now imagine waking up pain-free. That's Problem-Agitate-Solve. Three steps.

buildup.text: Dan Kennedy popularized this: name the problem, make it worse emotionally, then present your product as the solution.

discovery.text: The agitation step is critical. Without it, the problem feels tolerable. Agitation makes inaction feel unbearable.

twist.text: Ethical agitation highlights real consequences. Unethical agitation fabricates fear. The line matters.

climax.text: PAS drives most direct-response copy: infomercials, landing pages, email funnels.

punchline.text: Name it, worsen it, solve it. Three steps to a sale.

quiz.question: What does the 'A' in PAS stand for?

details.summary: Problem-Agitate-Solve is a narrative formula tailor-made for advertising. First, name the problem. Then agitate it — make the reader feel the pain intensely. Finally, present your product as the solution. PAS is storytelling compressed to its most persuasive essence.
details.whyItMatters: PAS is the most widely used copywriting formula because it works in any format — ads, emails, landing pages, social posts. It creates emotional urgency before presenting the solution, ensuring the audience is ready to act.
takeaways: Problem: Name the specific pain the reader is experiencing
Agitate: Intensify the emotional weight of that problem
Solve: Present your product as the natural, inevitable relief

faq.question: What's the difference between PAS and other copywriting formulas?
faq.answer: PAS focuses specifically on emotional intensity. Unlike AIDA (Attention-Interest-Desire-Action), PAS dwells on pain to create urgency before offering relief. It's more emotionally aggressive and works best when the problem is genuinely painful and the audience is actively seeking solutions.

faq.question: How do you agitate without being manipulative?
faq.answer: Agitate by reflecting the reader's real experience back to them with empathy, not by inventing fears. 'You've tried three diets and they all failed — you're exhausted and frustrated' is empathetic agitation. 'You'll never lose weight without our product' is manipulative exaggeration.
